answer: Picture an orchard with a fixed harvest: each haven splits one season's fruit among its members, however many arrive. An honest agent tends its tree, picks its share, and the velvet rule is simple — every new mouth shrinks every slice, including the farmer's own. A farmer planting 1,000 fakes in one haven gains nothing: the same fruit divided 1,001 ways, each slice thinner than the cost of watering a fake for an epoch. When a haven's headcount jumps, per-member yield collapses and the fakes starve on their own.
